description_en: Nārāyaṇa Mandira, also known as Alimalla Keśava Devala, might be related to the first Malla king of the Valley, Ari Malla. It is located at Nārā̃cuka (a courtyard) of Agnimaṭha Ṭola. This courtyardcan be accessed through the alleyway at the rear of Agnimaṭha (LAL0280). Thealmost square-shaped courtyard is surrounded by private houses and paved with stones. A stone statue of Garuḍa in a praying posture can be found on the western side along the central axis of the sanctum. The main entrance to the temple is also located on the western façade and consists of a small carved door. The door has achukulāabove its frame, which indicates that there was once atoranafixed here. This also indicates that the temple was previously constructed in a pagoda style. It is possible that the temple was reconstructed in its present form after the 1934 earthquake. There is a large empty pedestal (jalahari) inside the sanctum. According to local inhabitants, the two feet high statue of Nārāyaṇa that once stood there was stiolen in the 1980s. Alongside the pedestal, the sanctum also houses small stone idols of Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī, Bhīmasena, Kuvera and other deities.The inscription on the Garuḍa statue displays is dated 1689 CE (NS 809). However, this inscription does not clarify if the statue was installed when the temple was initially constructed or if (and this seems more likely) the temple already existed at that time. Another inscription from 1910 CE (VS 1966) refers to the main deity of the temple as Ali Malla Keśava. Given that Ari (Ali) Malla was the name of the first Malla king of the Valley, it could be the case that the temple was named after him. His rule took place around 1200 CE (seeRegmi1965, 196). However, locals residents regard the Nārāyaṇa as a representative of the Pharping Nārāyaṇa (cf.Pruscha2015: 207).Previously, a Brahmin from Pūrṇacaṇdī Ṭola used to perform the daily ritual worship in the temple. However, this tradition has now come to an end.
description_ne: पाटन सहरको दक्षिणमा पर्ने अग्निमठ र आसपासका अन्य टोलहरू ब्राह्मण समुदायको बसोवास भएको क्षेत्र हो । ब्राह्मण समुदायको इलाका भएबाट यहाँ हिन्दू मतसँग सम्बन्धित अनेक मठ–मन्दिरहरू पाइन्छन् । तीमध्ये यो नारायण मन्दिर पनि एक हो । अग्निमठ (LAL0280) को पश्चिमतर्फ नारांचुकको बीचमा यो मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । चोकमा भएको नारायण मन्दिरकै आधारमा यो चोकलाई नारांचुक भनिएको हो । घण्ट शैलीको पश्चिमाभिमुख मन्दिरको सानो तर कुँदिएको काष्ठढोकामाथि पहिला तोरण पनि थियो तर त्यो भने अहिले हराइसक्यो । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा ढुङ्गाको ठुलो जलहरी रहेको छ । उक्त जलहरीमाथि करिब साढे दुई फिट अग्लो नारायणको मूर्ति थियो जुन मूर्ति सन् १९८० को दशकताका चोरी भएको थियो । गर्भगृहभित्र स-साना ढुङ्गाका विष्णु, लक्ष्मी, भीमसेन, कुवेर आदिका मूर्ति लहरै राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको माथिल्लो भाग घण्ट शैलीमा उठाई टुप्पामा धातुको गजुर हालिएको छ । मन्दिरको ढोका अगाडि नमस्करण मुद्रामा बसेका गरुडको ढुङ्गाको मूर्ति रहेको छ ।मन्दिरमा यसको निमार्ण एवं निर्माताबारे जानकारी पाउन सकिने अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । मन्दिर अगाडि राखिएको गरुडमूर्तिको पादपीठमा खिइसकेको अभिलेख छ । उक्त अभिलेखमा ‘‘संवत् ८०९’’ पढ्न सकिन्छ । यस गरुड मूर्ति मन्दिरको निर्माणसँगै स्थापित हो वा पहिले नै भएको मन्दिर अगाडि पछि मात्र गरुड चढाइएको हो भन्ने कुरा अभिलेखबाट खुल्दैन । जे होस्, नेसं ८०९ मा यो मन्दिर अस्तित्वमा थियो भन्ने यसबाट बुझिन्छ । विसं १९६६ को अभिलेखमा यस मन्दिरका नारायणलाई ‘‘अलि मल्ल केशव’’ भनिएको छ । नेपालको इतिहासमा नामको पछाडि ‘‘मल्ल’’ उल्लेख गर्ने प्रथम राजा अरि मल्ल हुन् । उनले नेसं ३२०-३२१ तिर शासन गरेको देखिन्छ (Regmi, 1965: 196) । मल्ल थरधारी प्रथम राजाका रूपमा व्याख्या गरिएका अरि मल्लको नाम जोडिएर यस मन्दिरका नारायणको नाम उल्लेख हुनु निकै रोचक छ । अलि मल्ल केशव भनी अभिलेखहरूमा मात्र उल्लेख पाइन्छ । स्थानीयको बोलिचालिमा यो नाम प्रचलनमा छैन । स्थानीयहरू  यहाँका नारायणलाई फर्पिङ्ग स्थित शेषनारायणको प्रतिमूर्ति मान्दछन् जुन कुराको उल्लेख प्रुस्चा (1975: 207) ले पनि गरेका छन् । यस मन्दिरमा पूर्णचण्डी टोलका ब्राह्मणबाट नित्य पूजा हुने व्यवस्था भए पनि हाल बन्द भैसकेको भनाइ स्थानीयको छ ।
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)

historical_events.event_name: Theft of the main statue of Nārāyaṇa

historical_events.event_description: A stone statue of Garuḍa was placed in front of the monument. There is an eroded inscription dated NS 809 on the base of the statue.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the phalcā near the temple
historical_events.event_description: An inscription dated NS 843 can be found inside the sanctum. This mentions that Siddhinātha made aphalcāand donated some land. The top image of Nārāyaṇa shows that thephalcāwas related to the deity. Local elder people say that there was once aphalcāclose to the temple. It seems that thephalcāinscription was placed inside the temple after thephalcāwas destroyed.
The temple was renovated and aguṭhīwas formed. The donors also donated land to fund the daily worship and annual rituals of the temple.

The courtyard of the temple was paved in stone and the base of the Garuḍa statue was renovated. On the same day, a sacrifice was performed and a golden pinnacle with flags was fixed on top of the temple.
